On it. Quick findings from the first 15m of logs and metrics:

- Eviction rate on KV pool gpux-12 has doubled since 08:45 (evictions/sec from 18 -> 44).
- Hot-key hit ratio fell for several BrightPath prefixes; cold-start requests are causing high KV misses and backpressure into the serving pipeline.
- Batch lane usage: we see large batches filling the low-latency lane due to prefix misrouting; this triggers HOL blocking for concurrent small requests.
- Error pattern: majority of 5xx are GatewayTimeout / 504 from our router after KV timeouts (suggests long tail reads to backend).

Immediate mitigation plan (minutes to apply):
1) Flip eviction policy on affected pool from adaptive-LRU -> LFU-pref (reduces churn on frequently accessed keys).
   - Command: apply-config kv.pool.gpux-12.eviction=lfu_pref
   - Rationale: LFU will retain hot prefixes longer and reduce prefix-churn thrash.
2) Increase prefetched TTL for BrightPath prefixes from 6s -> 20s (temporary bump) to reduce cold misses.
   - Command: kv.prefetch.ttl.override[brightpath]=20s
3) Isolate batch lanes: add a quick policy to cap batch size for low-latency lane to 8 tokens and enable batch-lane throttling to prevent single large requests from starving lane.
   - Command: runtime.batch.lane.low_latency.max_batch=8
4) Spin a canary with the above changes on 2 nodes in us-west-2, monitor p99 and eviction rate for 10 minutes before rolling.

I'll push kv_eviction_patch.diff (small config patch) to the canary, apply the TTL override, and report back. If p99 recovers we roll to the pool. If not, fallback is to offload BrightPath to a reserved lane (increase cost but immediate SLA relief).

Jonas
Principal Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: UPDATE: BrightPath latency/error incident — mitigation applied and next steps

Sara / BrightPath team — quick update and timeline. TL;DR: applied targeted KV and batching changes to reduce eviction churn and eliminate HOL blocking; p99 and errors have returned to acceptable levels.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:40 — detected eviction churn and batch-lane congestion on gpux-12 impacting BrightPath prefixes.
- 09:46 — deployed canary config (kv_eviction_patch.diff): switched eviction to LFU-pref and increased prefetch TTL for BrightPath prefixes (6s -> 20s). Also limited low-latency batch size to 8 tokens.
- 09:57 — observed p99 drop from ~2.3s -> ~340ms within the canary nodes and eviction rate halved.
- 10:12 — rolled changes to whole gpux-12 pool. Error rate fell from ~6% -> 0.6% over the subsequent hour.
- 16:00 — final verification across US clusters, metrics stable (p99 ~280-320ms; 5xx < 0.5%; throughput steady). See attached p99_timeline_brightpath.png for before/after.

Why this happened (short):
- Root cause is operational: prefix-access patterns from BrightPath created hot-key pressure while our adaptive eviction and batch routing allowed large requests to occupy low-latency lanes. The combination produced eviction thrash and HOL blocking, causing KV misses and router timeouts.

Actions we took (next steps):
- Short term (applied): LFU-pref eviction, TTL bump for BrightPath prefixes, low-latency batch cap, canary then pool roll.
- Mid term (planned, next 7 days): add smarter prefix-aware prefetching (per-customer TTL heuristics), implement explicit lane isolation for high-throughput tenants, and add automated eviction alarms to detect early churn.
- Postmortem: scheduled for Wed 2026-05-20 10:00 PT. We'll include a detailed timeline, root cause, and permanent prevention steps.

Compensation / exec note: Marissa recommends a 10% usage credit to BrightPath for customer impact. If you agree, we'll prepare a formal credit and include it in the post-incident package.

Thanks for the quick coordination and apologies for the disruption — Mina on behalf of the ops team.
